summary.text: Roxanne Persaud is the incumbent Democratic state senator for District 19 in Brooklyn. Born in Guyana, she worked in higher-education administration and held several community posts before serving in the State Assembly and then winning a 2015 special election for the Senate. She chairs the Senate Social Services Committee and is the only candidate listed on the November 3, 2026 ballot for the seat.

paragraphs.text: Roxanne Persaud was born in Guyana, South America, and migrated to the United States with her parents and siblings; she lives in the Canarsie section of the 19th Senatorial District.
She graduated from Pace University, where she earned a Bachelor of Science and a Master of Science in Education Administration.
Before entering the legislature, she worked in higher-education administration, according to her official Senate biography.

She served as President of the 69th Precinct Community Council in Canarsie, a member of Community Board 18, and a Commissioner on the New York City Districting Commission, and she also served on the Community Action Board of the NYC Department of Youth and Community Development and chaired the Neighborhood Advisory Board for District 18.

Her official biography also lists graduation from the NYPD Citizens Police Academy and the NYC Office of Emergency Management's Community Emergency Response Team program, and overseas volunteer work on medical and social outreach programs.
Persaud was elected to the State Assembly's 59th District in the November 2014 general election and took office in 2015.

In November 2015 she won the special election for the State Senate's 19th District, defeating Republican Jeffrey J. Ferretti and Conservative Elias J. Weir; the seat had been vacant since John L. Sampson was removed from office on July 24, 2015.

In the 2025-2026 session she chairs the Senate Social Services Committee and also sits on the Children and Families, Cities 1, Codes, Disabilities, New York City Education, and Transportation committees, the Joint Senate Task Force on Opioids, Addiction & Overdose Prevention, and the Legislative Women's Caucus.
